description: CyberSentinel log pattern signatures for attack detection

patterns.name: SSH Brute Force Attack
patterns.description: Repeated failed authentication attempts targeting SSH service on port 22. Attacker is systematically trying username and password combinations.
log_indicators: Multiple 'Failed password for' entries from same source IP in short time window
Multiple 'Invalid user' entries from same source IP
'error: maximum authentication attempts exceeded' from same source IP
Linux auth.log entries showing repeated failures followed by account lockout

patterns.name: RDP Brute Force Attack
patterns.description: Repeated failed authentication attempts targeting Remote Desktop Protocol on port 3389. Common attack vector for ransomware deployment.
log_indicators: Multiple failed RDP connection attempts from same IP
Windows Event ID 4625 with Logon Type 10 (RemoteInteractive)
Multiple DROP rules triggered for port 3389 from same source

patterns.name: Aggressive Port Scan
patterns.description: Automated scanning of many ports in rapid succession. Indicates attacker is mapping your attack surface using tools like Nmap or Masscan.
log_indicators: Same source IP connecting to more than 20 different destination ports within 60 seconds
SYN packets to sequential port numbers without completing handshake
Multiple BLOCK/DROP entries for same source IP across diverse destination ports

patterns.name: Stealth Port Scan (Low and Slow)
patterns.description: Slow, deliberate port scanning spread over hours to avoid rate-based detection. Harder to detect but still discoverable via IP-based correlation.
log_indicators: Same source IP appearing across many different ports spread over hours
Low frequency of connections but high diversity of destination ports from same IP
Connection attempts at irregular intervals to avoid pattern detection

thresholds.suspicious: 20 different ports from same IP over 24 hours
thresholds.confirmed_attack: 50 different ports from same IP over 24 hours

patterns.name: Sensitive Service Port Probe
patterns.description: Targeted connection attempt to a sensitive or dangerous port. Even a single probe to certain ports warrants investigation.
log_indicators: Any connection attempt to database ports from external IPs: 3306, 5432, 1433, 27017, 6379, 1521
Connection attempt to admin or management ports: 8080, 8443, 9200, 4848
Connection attempt to legacy dangerous protocols: Telnet (23), FTP (21), SNMP (161)

sensitive_ports.23: Telnet - unencrypted remote admin, should never be exposed
sensitive_ports.445: SMB - Windows file sharing, common ransomware vector
sensitive_ports.6379: Redis - often has no authentication by default

patterns.name: Potential Data Exfiltration
patterns.description: Large or unusual outbound data transfer suggesting sensitive data may be leaving the network without authorization.
log_indicators: Outbound data transfer significantly exceeding baseline for that system or user
Large file transfers to previously unseen external IP addresses
Outbound traffic to cloud storage services from systems that do not normally use them
DNS queries for unusually long domain names suggesting DNS tunneling
Outbound connections on non-standard ports carrying large payloads

thresholds.review: Outbound transfer greater than 100MB in single session to new destination
thresholds.alert: Outbound transfer greater than 500MB in single session
thresholds.critical: Outbound transfer greater than 1GB or transfer to known threat actor infrastructure

patterns.name: Repeated Blocked Connection Attempts
patterns.description: Single source IP being blocked many times. May indicate a persistent attacker, misconfigured system, or compromised device attempting to connect.
log_indicators: More than 20 BLOCK or DROP entries for same source IP in firewall logs
Repeated connection attempts from same IP after being blocked
Same IP targeting multiple internal destination IPs

thresholds.suspicious: 20 blocked attempts in any time window
thresholds.high: 100 blocked attempts in any time window
thresholds.critical: 500 blocked attempts or spread across multiple destination IPs

patterns.name: Credential Stuffing Attack
patterns.description: Attacker using lists of breached username and password pairs to attempt access. Differs from brute force in that each attempt uses a different username.
log_indicators: Failed login attempts targeting many different usernames from same source IP
Failed attempts across multiple accounts using common passwords
Login attempts using email addresses as usernames from single IP

thresholds.suspicious: Failed attempts against 5 different usernames from same IP
thresholds.confirmed: Failed attempts against 20 different usernames from same IP
